what_matters.head: OCBC fell 5.8% by 12:05 SGT after Citi cut it to sell from neutral this morning, with a S$27.50 target.
what_matters.detail: Citi expects OCBC's third-quarter profit to be flat on a year earlier. The same note kept DBS at buy and UOB at sell. OCBC was the most-traded stock by value, and the three banks' weight pulled the Straits Times Index down 1.42% near noon.

what_matters.head: Samsung's preliminary third-quarter results are due Thursday; memory shares fell ahead of them.
what_matters.detail: Reuters: the analysts' average (LSEG) puts operating profit at about nine times a year earlier, but that average has been cut 7.7% since late August as memory-price rises slowed and the won rose 14.3% against the US dollar in the quarter. SK Hynix's US-listed shares fell 6.4% on Tuesday; Investing.com and 24/7 Wall St. cited the stronger won, bigger staff-bonus provisions and reports of US data-centre delays. Full results come in late October.

what_matters.head: Micron's Taiwan union strike vote closed Tuesday; no result had been published by 12:50 SGT today.
what_matters.detail: Searched CNA, UDN, Liberty Times, Commercial Times, Focus Taiwan and Taipei Times. A pass needs yes votes from more than half of all members and gives a right to strike, not a date. Micron's board is reported to review Taiwan profit-sharing options on 8 Oct, US time.

latest.tape_note: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq closed at records as oil steadied and Treasury yields eased. Chips were split: Broadcom rose after Marvell raised its long-term forecast, while memory names fell before Korea's results, so SOXX ended flat. The 10-year yield fell 4bp to 5.27%. The dollar index fell 0.3%, the biggest markets move against its usual day (1.1× usual); the US dollar slipped 0.15% against the Singapore dollar. Gold rose 0.7%; oil was flat.
